function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – Cell Phone Use | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs give priority to the vehicle already in the intersection. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or low visibility.
• Fog lights may only be used when visibility is less than 200 ft. | TxDOT – Headlight Rules | | **Towing & Tow‑Laws** | • Towing vehicles must have a tow‑bar or tow‑hook.
• The towing vehicle must be properly marked and equipped with a warning triangle. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a handicap space requires a valid permit. | TxDOT – Parking Regulations | | **School Bus** | • All vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading or unloading children.
• The bus must display its stop sign and flashing lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not change lanes in a “no‑change” zone. | TxDOT – Lane‑Changing Rules | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Vehicles must be registered and carry proof of insurance.
• Failure to register or insure can result in fines and impoundment. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras are used in many counties; fines are issued automatically. | TxDOT – Traffic Enforcement | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Roadside Assistance & Accident Reporting** | • Report accidents involving injury, death, or property damage over $1,000 to the police. | TxDMV – Accident Reporting | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT Website** – Regular updates on road conditions, construction, and new regulations. - **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text; available online through the Texas Legislature’s website. - **Local County Courts** – For specific traffic violations and court procedures. - **Texas DMV** – For registration, licensing, and insurance requirements. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always keep your headlights on** during low‑visibility conditions. 2. **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. 3. **Check speed limits** before entering a new county or city. 4. **Be extra cautious** around school zones and pedestrian crossings. 5. **Carry proof of insurance** and registration in your vehicle at all times. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to check the latest updates, let me know!
